With regard to the second issue, please be informed that cases where lhe validity of an Ordinance duly passed by the local sanggunian is being assailed, the Department has consistently upheld the presumpcion of validity in favor of th ordinance, in consonance with jurisprudence that: "It is a settled rule that an ordinanc enjoys the presumption of validity" (Social Justice Socieey• (SJS), Vladimir Alarique T Cabigao and Bonifacio S Tumbokon versus Hon. Jose L. Atienza, G.R. No. 156052, Febru ry 13, 2008, citing Vera vs. Hon. Judge Arca, 138 Phil. 369, In the case of "Ermita-WI-alate Hotel and Motel Operaors Association, Inc. vs. City Mayor of Manila", (20 SCRA 849), the Supreme Court was rather;emphatic, thus: 'Pfimarily what calls for a reversal of such decision is the absence of' any evidence to ofßet the presumption of validity that attaches to a challenged statute or ordinance. s was expressed categorically by Justice Malcolm: . "The presumption is all in favor of validity. x x x The ac,ion of the elected representatl es of the people cannot be lightly set aside. The councilors must, in e very nature of things, be familiar the necessities of their parti ular municipality and with all the facts and circumstances which surro d the subject and necessitate action. The local legislative body, by enacting the ordinance, has in effect given notice that the regulations are essential to the well- being of the people. x x x. " And in San Miguel Brewery, Inc. vs. Magno, (21 SCR+ 293), it was held that: "A municipal ordinance is not suffect to collateral attack. Public policy forbids collateral impeachment of legislative acts. " Finally, in "Mayor Nbrberto M. Mendoza vs. Abstenen ia de Guzman, et al. G.R. Nos. 156697-98, 09 October 2007, the newly-elected mayor o Naujan, Oriental Mindoro, questioned the validity of an Ordinance enacted by the previous et of Sangguniang Bayan on the ground that it was not deliberated on by the aforesaid leg •slative body in violation of

Article 107, Rule 17 of the Rules and Regulations Implementing hhe Local Government Code of 1991. The Supreme Court ( Fan Banc) through an extended deci ion, held and we quote: "To reiterate, a petition for mandamus is not the eroperproceeding to raise the invalidity 01' che questioned Ordinance. It as been held that when a municipal corporation has the power to enact an ordinance but does so in an unauthorized mode, the Ordinance is s I legally binding until judicially held ocbervvise. The validity of the Or • ance cannot be questioned collaterally as a matter of defense to an action under it. Whether the Ordinance was indeed a falsified do ument must be resolved in a separate action. This would afford the groper parties the opportunity to prove the validity of' the Ordinance an appropriate proceeding. Until thus resolved, the Ordinance in uestion enjoys a presumption of validity, and petitioner as incumben mayor is duty- bound to implement it. j' In this particular case, ic appears that Ordinance No. 94-2001 has neither been repealed nor invalidated by the proper court under these cir umstances, it should be accorded the presumption of validity like any ordinance passed b the City of Antipolo.
